examShortTricks: Trick 1: Magical realism: the angel is treated with mundane boredom (chickens, spider sideshow) — the extraordinary rendered ordinary is the genre's signature; define it with one example.
Trick 2: Satire of human cruelty and credulity: villagers charge to see him, pluck feathers, then forget him — collect two acts of cruelty.
Trick 3: The spider-woman outdraws the angel because her story has a MORAL — the satire on audiences preferring clear lessons to mystery; explain this comparison.
practiceQuestions: Q. How do the villagers treat the angel? (2 marks) — as a carnival curiosity: caged in the chicken coop, charged admission, poked with iron.
Q. Why does the spider-woman attract more visitors than the angel? (2 marks) — her clear moral tale is easier to consume than the angel's silent mystery.
keyPoints: Magical realism: the angel treated as a sideshow — miracle meets mundane cruelty.
Compare with the spider-woman: people prefer a moral story to a mystery.
